name: Ch'ol
variant: Ch'ol of Tila and Tumbalá, INALI writing standard
region: Northern Chiapas (Tila, Tumbalá, Salto de Agua, Palenque, Sabanilla) and parts of Tabasco and Campeche, in Mexico
summary: The Mayan language of the Ch'ol people of northern Chiapas, neighbours of Palenque. Its verb marks who something happens to in two ways, depending on whether the action is finished or not.

conjugator.label: Verb
conjugator.hint: Type an intransitive verb with -el (majlel «go», wäyel «sleep») or the root of a transitive one (k'ux «eat something», mek' «hug»). You can also type just the root (majl).

own.hint: Type a verb ending in -el (intransitive) or a transitive root, and its meaning in English. In the perfective, transitives take their root's own vowel: k'ux → k'uxu.

source.short: Warkentin and Scott, Gramática ch'ol (1980); Aulie, Diccionario ch'ol (2009); INALI, writing standard
source.full: Viola Warkentin and Ruby Scott, Gramática ch'ol (Summer Institute of Linguistics, 1980), for the verb: aspects, future, perfect, imperative and persons; H. Wilbur Aulie and Evelyn W. de Aulie, Diccionario ch'ol de Tumbalá, Chiapas, con variaciones dialectales de Tila y Sabanilla (SIL, 3rd ed., 2009), and its grammar, for the participles, the imperative and vocabulary; Jessica Coon, «Ch'ol», in Judith Aissen, Nora England and Roberto Zavala (eds.), The Mayan Languages (2015 draft, drawing on Juan Jesús Vázquez Álvarez, A Grammar of Chol, 2011), for split ergativity; INALI, Ityoj ts'ijbuñtyel lakty'añ ch'ol: norma de escritura de la lengua ch'ol, for the spelling, into which we rewrite every form from the SIL sources (c, qu, ʌ → k, ä); Miguel Sánchez Álvarez (coord.), CHajpäbilbä tsolty'añ tyi lakty'añ: vocabulario de la lengua ch'ol (UNICH, 2013), for vocabulary and examples (tsa' majliyoñ, mi kmajlelojoñ, tsa' la'amele); also Enrique Jiménez Jiménez and Jorge Guzmán Gutiérrez, Its'ijbuñtyel ña'alty'añ Ch'ol (INALI, 2013), and the Cuaderno de trabajo chol (SIL and SEP, 1974).

about: Ch'ol is a Mayan language of northern Chiapas, spoken in Tila, Tumbalá, Salto de Agua, Palenque and Sabanilla, and by communities that moved to Tabasco and Campeche. It has some two hundred thousand speakers, who call it lakty'añ, «our word».

It belongs to the Ch'olan branch, with Ch'orti' and Ch'olti', the language of many Classic Maya hieroglyphic inscriptions; this is why epigraphers study Ch'ol to read the inscriptions of Palenque. It has two main varieties, Tila and Tumbalá.
It is taught in bilingual schools and has an INALI writing standard. Radio, music and vocabularies made with speakers, such as the one by the Intercultural University of Chiapas, keep it alive.

orthography.intro: We use the INALI writing standard, the one of the Vocabulario de la lengua ch'ol. Consonants with an apostrophe are glottalized, ty and ñ are palatal, and the sixth vowel is written ä.
notes: ä is a central vowel, between i and u, like ɨ: chäy «fish». It comes from an old short a; its neighbours Tseltal and Tsotsil don't have it.
After a vowel, j marks a vowel that ends in a breath: sak' «stinging» and sajk' «grasshopper» differ only in this.
ty and ñ are palatal, like the t in a quick «tune» and the ñ in «niño»; Ch'ol has almost no plain t or n. That is why the perfective is heard as tsa' or ta'.
At the start of a sentence or a name, double letters take two capitals: CHa'añ, TYi, TSa'. The apostrophe and the hyphen mark the glottal stop.
Older spellings, such as that of the Summer Institute of Linguistics, write ty as ẗ or t'y, and ä as ʌ or i̱.

grammar.intro: A Ch'ol verb follows an aspect word (tsa' perfective, mi imperfective, chonkol progressive) and carries two sets of person markers: Set A, prefixes (k-, a-, i-), and Set B, suffixes (-oñ, -ety, Ø). The future is made with mi kej, and the perfect with a participle: majlemoñ «I have gone». Words like ak'bi «yesterday» and ijk'äl «tomorrow» place things in time.

items.description: tsa' perfective, mi imperfective, chonkol progressive.
k- / j- I, a- / aw- you, i- / y- he or she, lak- we (with you), la'a- / la'aw- you all.
-i intransitive perfective, -el imperfective, -em participle, -V transitive perfective, -Vñ derived.

blocks.title: Two alignments
blocks.description: In the perfective and the perfect, the subject of an intransitive is marked like the object of a transitive, with Set B. In the imperfective and progressive, it is marked like the subject of a transitive, with Set A.

blocks.title: Two «we»
blocks.description: lak- and -oñla include the listener; -lojoñ leaves them out, and after an l it is written -ojoñ. For «you all» Set A is la'a- and Set B -etyla; the 3rd person plural is -ob. The Norma also allows kwäyela «we (with you) sleep» and awäyela «you all sleep».

blocks.title: Every affix of the verb
blocks.description: Every piece a Ch'ol verb can take: aspect and negation words in front, Set A as a prefix, the root with its status suffix, Set B and the plural clitics at the end, and the suffixes that make new verbs.

items.meaning: imperfective: habit or what will happen
not, with the verb in its dependent form
I: transitive subject; intransitive subject outside the perfective
I: object; intransitive subject in the perfective
transitive in the perfective: the root's vowel (a gives ä, except after j)
intransitive perfect, with Set B (-eñ after m)

tenses.name: Perfective
tenses.description: What already happened, the finished action (tsa'). Intransitives take -i and Set B; transitives, their root's vowel.

tenses.name: Perfective with -ix
tenses.description: What has already happened: tsa' plus the clitic -ix «already».

tenses.name: Imperfective
tenses.description: What always, usually or will happen (mi). Intransitives take Set A and -el.

tenses.name: Progressive
tenses.description: What is happening now (chonkol; in Tumbalá, woli).

tenses.name: Future
tenses.description: What will happen: mi kej (in Tumbalá, mi kaj) and the verb as in the imperfective.

tenses.name: Perfect
tenses.description: What has happened and still holds. Intransitives take the participle -em (-eñ after m) with Set B; transitives, the participle -äl and cha'añ with Set A (in Tumbalá, -bil).

tenses.name: Pluperfect
tenses.description: What had already happened before something else: the perfect with -ix.

tenses.name: Imperative
tenses.description: Commands. Intransitives take -en; transitives, their vowel as in the perfective, but derived ones keep the -ñ. The plural adds -la.
